citation.title: Imputation of faulty magnetic sensors with coupled Bayesian and Gaussian processes to reconstruct the magnetic equilibrium in real time
citation.authors: S. Joung, J. Kim, S. Kwak, K.-r. Park, S. H. Hahn, H. S. Han, H. S. Kim, J. G. Bak, S. G. Lee, Y.-c. Ghim
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1063/1.5038938 (this paper's own DOI; PDF p1 cover, p2 abstract)

scope_read.pdf_pages: 1-6 (p1 publisher cover; p2-6 article, Figs 1-4, Eqs 1-12)
scope_read.limitations: Proceedings paper. Results are shown only as figures, with no error metrics or tables. Hardware and timing method are unspecified.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: 'Real time' means a deployed real-time system.
claim_checks.source_finding: The authors state the method runs in under 1 ms on a typical personal computer. Integration into a plasma control system is not shown. Real-time fault detection is attributed to cited works (refs 6,7) and was not implemented here. Real-time hyperparameter search is listed as future work.
claim_checks.locator: p2 abstract; p5 Sec II C after Eq 12; p6 Sec II C three-step list and Sec III
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: On KSTAR, a Maxwell-constrained Bayesian model coupled with a Gaussian process over probe positions was used to impute missing magnetic-probe signals, with computation reported below 1 ms on a personal computer [Joung2018].
claim_checks.qualification: 'Real time' here refers to computation latency. Deployment is not shown.

claim_checks.source_finding: The GP-only scheme is shown with nine non-consecutive Bt and Bn signals removed at 3.70 s of shot #9010. The coupled Bayes+GP scheme is shown with two removed signals (Bt #15/#16; Bn #17/#18) at 0.1 s, plus single-probe time traces for shot #9427. The abstract and conclusion state that nine signals are handled, but no figure shows the coupled method with nine.
claim_checks.locator: p4 Fig 3(a,b); p5 Fig 4(a-d); p2 abstract; p6 Sec III
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: The authors examined up to nine simultaneously removed, non-consecutive probe signals [Joung2018].
claim_checks.qualification: Attribute the nine-signal result to the examples shown (GP-only in Fig 3). Do not assign it to the coupled method as a demonstrated result.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Physics constraint plus local GP prior resolves the shortcomings of each component alone.
claim_checks.source_finding: Ampère's law and Gauss's law each give one equation, so two or more missing signals of one component leave the problem underdetermined (Fig 2). GP-only inference fails for spatially fast-varying probes and during current ramp-up and ramp-down. The coupled scheme tracks the measured signals in the cases shown.
claim_checks.locator: p3 Eqs 1-5; p4 Fig 2, Fig 3(c,d); p5 Eqs 8-12, Fig 4
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: In that work, combining a single physical constraint with a spatial GP prior made multi-signal imputation determinable [Joung2018].
claim_checks.qualification: This is shown qualitatively, for a few shots and time slices.

input_target_timing.inputs: Same-time intact probe Bt/Bn; probe R,Z positions; Rogowski Ip; PF-coil contributions; up-down paired probe value (prior mean)
input_target_timing.outputs: Missing probe values at the same time slice
input_target_timing.causal_or_offline: Instantaneous spatial imputation with no temporal model, evaluated offline on archived shots
input_target_timing.source_diagnostic_as_input: Yes: the other probes of the same diagnostic
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Imputed values are compared with measured probe signals that were artificially withheld; this is not physical truth

validation.independent_truth: No; withheld measurements serve as reference
validation.unknowns: Whether hyperparameters were fit on the evaluated shots; no quantitative metrics; number of shots evaluated; eddy-current effects excluded (flat-top assumption)

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Author-reported computation under 1 ms on a typical PC
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Hardware, timing distribution, PCS integration, end-to-end latency, closed-loop or EFIT use
runtime_or_deployment.locator: p5-6 Sec II C; p6 Sec III

forbidden_inferences: The method was deployed in KSTAR real-time control
The coupled method is demonstrated with nine missing signals
The method performs temporal or causal nowcasting
The method is relevant to CES or ion temperature
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. It is spatial, same-time imputation of magnetic probes using Maxwell constraints. Our work is temporal nowcasting of a CES report from past reports and BES/ECEI voltages. Cite it as KSTAR precedent for missing-diagnostic imputation where 'real time' means computation latency, not as a baseline.
